newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Democrats to support AN sale bill.
newsitem.headline: Australia Democrats to support AN sale bill.

text.p: The Australian Democrats minor party said on Monday it would agree to pass legislation for the sale of government-owned rail operator Australian National (AN).
But Democrats transport spokesman Andrew Murray said the party's support depended on the inclusion in the legislation of some safeguards.
"While the Democrats are prepared to allow the sale to proceed, it is only on the assurance that the government will continue to take an active, ongoing role in rail," Murray said in a statement.
He said the Democrats wanted to amend the legislation to include a guarantee that a National Track Authority would be established.
"The authority will own the track, which is a natural monopoly, backed up with a legislative guarantee that parliamentary approval will be required before it can be sold off," he said.
The Democrats also wanted a guarantee that the authority would be headquartered in the state of South Australia and that the government would restore funding for track upgrading.
The government late last year announced its intention to sell AN through a trade sale, which analysts expect to raise up to A$600 million.
In May, Finance Minister John Fahey said the government had drawn up a shortlist of about 12 companies interested in AN or some of its assets from more than 50 expressions of interest.
The government said last week final bids for the rail operator were expected by mid-July.
AN operates freight services and workshops in South Australia and Tasmania, in addition to three interstate passenger services. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
